articles.title: Mahua Moitra faces egg-attack in West Bengal's Tehatta
articles.summary: Eggs hurled at Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra in Tehatta; she blames BJP workers and alleges police inaction despite Calcutta High Court protection order.
articles.body: TEHATTA: Eggs were thrown at Trinamool Krishnanagar MP Mahua Moitra in Tehatta on Wednesday after she arrived in her constituency to attend a party meeting.Moitra alleged that seven to 10 BJP workers, including the local mandal president and the president and vice-president of the panchayat samiti, threw eggs at her after she came out of the first meeting of the day, even as police stood watching.On Sept 1, Calcutta High Court had directed police to deploy two personnel for a month to protect Moitra during her visits to her constituency, where eggs and stones have been pelted at her repeatedly since her party’s defeat in the assembly elections.On Sept 9, Moitra had written to Krishnanagar SP Atul V regarding her visit to Tehatta from Sept 15 to 17. On Sept 11, the SP wrote back stating she had been assigned a lady assistant sub-inspector to act as the nodal officer for her visit.Moitra did not face any trouble while reaching the meeting venue in Tehatta 1 block. The local inspector in charge, Supriya Ranjan Maji, however, claimed he was unaware of any meeting.In a video message posted on X, Moitra could be heard saying: “We are at Tehatta party office. You can see, we are under police protection, and the court has said no one will throw eggs. They brought eggs right in front of the police. Look at this, all of you. What is happening? Right in front of the police, they are trying to throw eggs… this is contempt of the high court.”“According to the court’s direction, four police personnel were with me. During the attack, more cops came, but instead of controlling the protesters, they forcibly put me into the car. This is what is happening in West Bengal! The high court has been saying this should not happen,” she added.At one point, Maji approached the MP, telling her to leave immediately while questioning why he was not informed about the meeting. Moitra told the officer that it was an indoor meeting and that she had arrived only after receiving the SP’s assurance.As Moitra boarded her SUV, she was hit with two eggs. Refusing to back off, she kept shouting slogans. Her nodal officer was seen pushing away an attacker who had approached her vehicle.Moitra headed to her next meeting, with broken eggshells stuck in her hair and her face smeared with egg.“It is important that people see what is happening in Bengal today. An MP is being attacked with police doing nothing. And this is after a Calcutta HC order. But if they think they can intimidate and scare me, or my party workers off, they have picked the wrong person and the party. We will continue to fight. And when the right time comes, they will have to pay back,” the MP said.In a statement, Moitra also referred to the Supreme Court’s observations while dismissing her plea seeking protection from such attacks.Denying his party’s involvement, Bengal BJP spokesperson Debjit Sarkar said, “Eggs being pelted at a woman… I condemn it if the claims are true. At the same time, it has to be seen whether she has made it all up. articles.title: Nigerian national who murdered his friend over a woman in Pune denied bail
articles.summary: Pune court denies bail to Nigerian national Nnsemeka Onyia, accused of murdering compatriot Yemeka Kristian in Pisoli; judge cites strong evidence, flight risk.
articles.body: PUNE: Additional Sessions Judge S D Kulkarni on Tuesday rejected the bail application of Nigerian national Nnsemeka Maduabuchi Onyia, 48, accused of murdering a compatriot during a late-night altercation in Pisoli in Jan, saying the prosecution had collected sufficient material linking him to the crime and there was a possibility of him fleeing from justice if released.Onyia was arrested on Jan 12 in connection with an FIR registered at Kalepadal police station under sections 103(1) and 3(5) of the BNS, Section 4(25) of the Arms Act and Sections 37(1) and 135 of the Maharashtra Police Act. The chargesheet has been filed, though no prosecution witness had been examined when the bail application was decided.The case relates to the death of Yemeka Kristian, 40, who was allegedly assaulted after a dispute during a dinner gathering at a Nigerian woman’s flat in Pisoli in the early hours of Jan 12. Police said the dispute was linked to a romantic relationship involving the woman. Kristian was taken to Ruby Hall Clinic after the assault but died while undergoing treatment. Police had registered a murder case against three Nigerian nationals and arrested Onyia and another accused while the third accused is still at large.The judge noted that the FIR named Onyia as an aggressor and that eyewitnesses allegedly stated that he took a sharp weapon from the kitchen, followed Kristian and assaulted him on vital parts of the body. The court also referred to medical papers showing multiple chop wounds and to the informant’s statement regarding an alleged statement made by Kristian before his death.The judge held that considering the gravity of the offence, the material against Onyia and the possibility of his fleeing to Nigeria, he was not entitled to bail.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: UP man beheads sleeping wife over ‘affair’, walks into police station
articles.summary: Hardoi: Parvez arrested for allegedly beheading wife Nagma over suspected affair; police investigating family abuse claims, probing relatives’ role, seeking weapon.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Suspecting his wife of having an affair, a man allegedly beheaded her while she was asleep at their rented house in Hardoi’s Islamnagar Tiliya locality early Wednesday, police said.The accused, identified as Parvez (34), was arrested after he reportedly walked into a police station and surrendered.The victim, Nagma (28), had been married to Parvez for nearly 12 years. According to police, the couple’s relationship had been strained for several months, with Parvez allegedly suspecting his wife of being in contact with another man on the phone. Frequent arguments reportedly took place over the issue.Investigators said Nagma was sleeping when Parvez allegedly attacked her with a sharp-edged weapon. Police said he repeatedly assaulted her before severing her head.The couple had been living in a rented house for the past one-and-a-half months after Parvez sold his ancestral property.Nagma’s sister, Sabbo, claimed that she had been subjected to prolonged physical abuse and threats by her husband. She alleged that Parvez had repeatedly threatened to slit Nagma’s throat in the days leading up to the murder. The family also alleged that some of Parvez’s relatives were present in the house when the crime took place.Nagma’s mother, Zahida, alleged that her daughter had faced repeated harassment and intimidation from her husband and in-laws.Police have sent the body for postmortem and launched an investigation. articles.title: Balaclava boys on electric bikes: How to tackle the problem?
articles.summary: The sight of masked young men on electric bikes or motorcycles is becoming increasingly familiar - what can be done about it?
articles.body:
From the Pentland Hills near Edinburgh to the streets of the country's biggest cities, a common menace is causing irritation, alarm and in some cases even death.

The sight of young men, their identities hidden by black balaclavas, tearing around on electric bikes or scooters is becoming a familiar one.

The picture above was taken by a man who posted on social media about "morons on electric bikes" scaring a nearby horse as they rode illegally on public footpaths.

Aside from being showered with gravel churned up by the "gobby" miscreants, no one came to harm that day, but others have not been so lucky.

Earlier this year, a court was shown distressing dashcam footage of the moment a masked 18-year-old on an electric motorbike ploughed into a woman on a pedestrian crossing in Sunderland.

Gloria Stephenson, 86, died at the scene. The rider - Billy Stokoe, who had taken cannabis and was using his mobile at the time of the crash - was jailed for more than six years for causing death by dangerous driving.

Few would dispute that illegal e-bikes and scooters are a growing problem, but what can be done about it? Here are some of the options.

The term e-bike is often used loosely to cover a range of different vehicles.

Strictly speaking it refers to an electrically assisted pedal cycle (an EAPC) where an electric motor kicks in to take the strain off the rider while pedalling.

By law, the motor cuts out at 15.5mph (25km/h) and its continuous power is capped at 250 watts.

But these safeguards are easily bypassed by "tuning kits" or software hacks that make them capable of running much faster, sometimes in excess of 40mph.

A quick search of online marketplaces reveals all sorts of modifications on offer, often shipped from eastern Europe, including motorbike-style twist grip throttles which allow the rider to accelerate without pedalling.

Then there are electric dirt bikes from manufacturers such as Sur-Ron which look like mountain bikes but are capable of about 50mph - and 70mph or more if modified.

Unlike legal e-bikes they require a licence and insurance to be used in public spaces or on roads.

E-scooters are also popular - despite it currently being illegal to ride them on public roads or pavements except in certain rental zones.

What they all have in common is that they are expensive, ranging from a few hundred to several thousands of pounds, and modifications can cost hundreds of pounds more on top.

Seizing and destroying them represents a significant penalty.

A new law and rules introduced this summer gave police in England and Wales greater powers to seize illegal vehicles, and without the need for a formal warning if they are being used in an anti-social manner.

They can also now be crushed within 48 hours.

In Scotland, ministers say they are in favour of increasing police seizure powers, although they point out bikes can already be seized under certain circumstances.

Catching the offenders is a problem for the police - it's a crime where its very nature means the suspects have a fast and highly manoeuvrable method of escape.

A patrol car can easily be evaded by heading down a narrow alleyway or through bollards. David Kennedy from the Scottish Police Federation says more dangerous tactics are also employed.

"These individuals on these bikes will come up one-way streets the wrong way so there's no way a police officer in a car or even on a motorbike would be safe to follow them," he told BBC Radio Scotland Breakfast.

Some forces across the UK have responded to the challenge by setting up specialised units backed up by drones

In parts of inner city London, Metropolitan Police officers have been equipped with a fleet of 25 Sur-Ron dirt bikes - partly funded with proceeds of crime money.

As part of a crackdown targeting mobile phone thefts - which in London often involve such bikes - they claim it has helped cut offences by 13,000 in a year.

A number of forces have successfully used drones to track illegal e-bike riders rather than engaging in risky pursuits.

Officers monitor suspects from above, then their colleagues are directed to move in on foot to make seizures and arrests.

In Devon and Cornwall officers have also sprayed illegal riders and their bikes with SmartWater - a forensic marking product that contains a unique chemical code which becomes visible using ultraviolet light.

One of the most sinister aspects of e-bike misuse is that riders often wear black balaclavas or "ballys".

Whether it is a practical attempt to hide their identity or part of a youth sub-culture, there is no doubt that many people find the sight of masked youths intimidating.

The debate about the appropriateness of wearing balaclavas in public places goes wider than e-bikes, encompassing anti-social behaviour, crime and some anti-immigration protests.

New restrictions introduced just this week under Operation Reclaim in Nottingham give police and council officers the power to order people to remove face coverings, backed up by £70 fixed penalty notices.

Exemptions apply for religious, medical and certain other legitimate reasons.

David Kennedy from the Scottish Police Federation says there is definitely "more to do" on face coverings although he cautions that localised enforcement might simply see youths moving elsewhere.

"If you are on an e-bike and you are wearing a face covering, the concern I have got is you are not wearing a helmet," he adds.

"I don't see many people travelling about the city centre on e-bikes wearing helmets."

Many parents are unaware that knowingly allowing their child to use an illegal e-bike or an e-scooter in a public place could land them with a fine or points on their driving licence.

Under the current law, e-scooters can only be used legally on private land.

The only exceptions are a number of rental trial zones, all of them located in England, yet some parents regard e-scooters as legitimate toys.

Riders of legal electrically assisted pedal bikes must be at least 14, and any illegal modification means the bikes qualify as a motor vehicle/moped, requiring registration, a driving licence, tax and insurance.

If an under-18-year-old is stopped by the police, their parents could potentially be accused of "causing or permitting" a driving offence with a possible £300 fine and six penalty points.

And even a child too young to drive can have points added to a "ghost licence" which can transfer to their provisional when they are old enough to apply for one.

Some argue the problems needs to be addressed earlier, before a young person gets hold of an e-bike or e-scooter, by targeting the point of sale.

This could range from clearer warnings about the rules, to a mandatory buyer information and registration scheme which would make it easier for police to trace vehicles used in crime or anti-social behaviour.

Last year an all-party Westminster inquiry called for action to close a legal loophole that allows illegal vehicles to be sold under the guise of off-road use.

The MPs also suggested that online marketplaces be held accountable for unsafe products such as the modification kits that are sold on their platforms.

Offer young people something better to do

Moral outrage at the behaviour of young people is nothing new and predates the invention of e-bikes by a considerable margin. Historians have found texts bemoaning declining standards dating back 4,000 years to ancient Mesopotamia.

Some might argue the e-bike scourge is just the latest manifestation of an age-old problem and that rather than demonising the "bally boys" a better approach is to try to understand the boredom and frustrations that underpin the trend.

In Aberdeen, alongside police enforcement action, one go karting centre is offering free sessions where e-scooter and e-bike riders can use them in a legal and safer environment.

But given the scale of e-bike misuse, can such schemes make an impact?

The backdrop is a long-term decline in services for young people and financial pressures on local authorities and charities that provide them.

A report from the YMCA last year found council-funded youth services in England and Wales have lost more than £1bn since 2010 with hundreds of youth clubs shutting and youth worker posts disappearing.

Whether the answer is drones, dedicated police units or creating more positive ways in which young people can fill their day, the common denominator is fresh thinking and - arguably the biggest challenge - extra resources.

articles.title: King's 'astonishing outburst' and 'heartbreak' after search for missing Noah
articles.summary: Several of today's papers splash on the Palace's response to Earl Spencer's claim in his upcoming book about his sister Diana.
articles.body:
The new allegations made in Earl Spencer's book are on several front pages. The Daily Mirror describes as "shocking" his claim that within days of Princess Diana's death the-then Prince Charles told him that she would be forgotten soon enough.

According to the Daily Telegraph a source close to the King says the alleged comment was "just not in his nature" especially not at that time when he was "absolutely grief-stricken".

The Palace's rejection of the claims is also on the Sun's front page, under the headline "Recollections may vary..... again."

The Times says the row between Earl Spencer and the King will be seen as a further crisis for the monarchy. The paper says the Royal Family is preparing for a series of allegations in the book.

People close to the artificial intelligence companies, Anthropic and OpenAI, have told the Financial Times that proposals - put forward in recent days by their bosses, on how to constrain AI's development - are creating tensions among staff.

The paper says one of the ideas is to embed outside evaluators within the labs to oversee model development, but some fear this could compromise the security of their prized technology.

Writing in the Daily Express , the Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, argues that Andy Burnham will drag Britain back into the 1970s. She says the government wants to spend more and tax more.

The i Paper highlights the prime minister's pledge that the government will exercise the "highest degree of prudence" in next month's Budget. The paper also says the Chancellor John Healey is likely to increase capital gains tax.

The Guardian reports that plans have been drawn up to "double up" prisoners in temporary prefabricated cells built for one person, because of a shortage of prison spaces in England and Wales.

The paper says using the prefabricated cells to house two inmates could increase the capacity of the prison estate by 476. The Ministry of Justice says it is "pulling every lever available" to ensure there is space to lock up dangerous offenders.

And finally the Daily Mail says it's spoken to outraged parents in Somerset after a new headteacher of Frome Community College suspended 25 pupils in the first week of term.

The headteacher Dan Jeffries says the punishments were for "persistent disruption," but some parents likened his strict regime to that on a military base.

images.caption: Earl Spencer, the brother of Diana, Princess of Wales, has ignited a fresh row with the Palace following claims in his upcoming book, which feature heavily in today's papers. The book claims that King Charles told Spencer in the days after Diana's death in 1997: "Rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough", the Times reports. The paper headlines on a Buckingham Palace official statement that hit back at the book, saying grief can "colour memory".

articles.title: Motorista ajudou a resgatar vereador que caiu no Rio Piracicaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Fabrício Polezi (PL) está internado em estado grave e respira com ajuda de aparelhos. Resgate nesta quarta (16) também mobilizou equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros e Samu.
articles.summary: Fabrício Polezi (PL) está internado em estado grave e respira com ajuda de aparelhos.
articles.body:
Um motorista de aplicativo ajudou a resgatar o vereador de Piracicaba (SP) Fabrício Polezi (PL), que caiu acidentalmente no Rio Piracicaba na manhã desta quarta-feira (16) e está internado em estado grave .

À EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo, Rafael de Oliveira Araújo contou que estava próximo ao rio aguardando uma corrida, quando presenciou a queda do vereador de uma ponte na região da Rua do Porto, ponto turístico da cidade.

"A gente fica apavorado. A gente vê que é uma vida. Na verdade, eu nem sabia que era um vereador. Não sabia, juro por Deus. Vi que caiu e que o rapaz estava precisando de ajuda."

Araújo explica que ele e um outro homem entraram no rio e puxaram o vereador, que estava inconsciente na hora do resgate.

"Vi que ele não estava afundando. A blusa acho que não deixava ele afundar, uma blusa de seda que ele estava. Vi que ele estava apagado, que ele não estava bem. Na hora, a gente pede força para Deus. Falei: 'eu sei nadar, vou pular, e nós vamos puxando ele'."

O motorista de aplicativo Rafael de Oliveira Araújo ajudou a resgatar o vereador de Piracicaba (SP) Fabrício Polezi, que caiu no Rio Piracicaba — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/EPTV

O parlamentar está internado na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) na Santa Casa de Misericórdia do município e respira com ajuda de aparelhos.

"Permanece sob sedação, ventilação mecânica e suporte intensivo, com acompanhamento contínuo da equipe médica", diz a Santa Casa.

O boletim médico foi divulgado às 16h desta quarta-feira. Segundo a nota, o estado grave é decorrente do comprometimento respiratório provocado pelo tempo em que o vereador ficou na água.

A Santa Casa ainda informou que todos os cuidados intensivos estão sendo adotados, mas que a evolução clínica será avaliada nas próximas horas, não sendo possível, neste momento, antecipar um prognóstico.

Santa Casa de Piracicaba — Foto: Claudia Assencio/g1

De acordo com as informações divulgadas pela Câmara Municipal, com base nos relatos do Corpo de Bombeiros, o acidente ocorreu enquanto o vereador registrava imagens na região da ponte sobre o rio. Em um momento de descuido, caiu na água e foi arrastado pela força da correnteza.

Polezi também recebeu os primeiros socorros de equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros e do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu).

Em nota oficial, a Mesa Diretora da Câmara Municipal de Piracicaba lamentou o ocorrido e informou que segue acompanhando de perto a situação do parlamentar.

"A Câmara Municipal acompanha a situação e, neste momento, manifesta sua solidariedade aos familiares do vereador, desejando a Fabrício Polezi plena recuperação", escreveu o Legislativo.

Fabrício Polezi (PL) durante tribuna na Câmara Municipal de Piracicaba — Foto: Rubens Cardia/Câmara de Piracicaba

articles.title: Seca no Bailique: Estudantes empurram barcos na lama para ir à escola | G1
articles.standfirst: Com os rios do arquipélago no Amapá no nível mínimo, embarcações do transporte escolar encalham e jovens enfrentam longos trajetos a pé e risco de ataques de raias para não perder as aulas.
articles.summary: Com a seca no Bailique, estudantes empurram barcos na lama e enfrentam riscos de ataques de arraias para conseguir chegar às escolas no Amapá.
articles.body:
A seca rigorosa no Arquipélago do Bailique, distrito a 180 km de Macapá , no Amapá , reduziu o nível dos rios e travou a navegação do transporte escolar, afetando a vida dos moradores de diversas comunidades da região.

Com a foz do Igarapé Grande tomada por bancos de lama, estudantes são obrigados a desembarcar, empurrar as embarcações motorizadas e fazer longas caminhadas a pé pela mata para conseguir chegar às salas de aula e retornar para casa.

"A gente faz esse mesmo trajeto todo dia: tem que empurrar a rabeta, mas ela não passa de tão seco que está. A gente anda na lama porque não tem outro jeito, a gente não pode fazer nada. Chega num ponto que não dá mais para ir de barco. A gente chega até numa certa distância e depois tem que entrar na mata para poder chegar na comunidade", relata a estudante Cheuda de Pinho, de 18 anos, em um vídeo gravado durante o trajeto.

Estudante Cheuda Batista de Pinho gravou um vídeo durante trajeto para a escola no Bailique. — Foto: Divulgação

Espera na margem e logística comprometida

Sem conseguir avançar pelos canais navegáveis, os alunos deixam os barcos encalhados na lama, caminham até uma casa de apoio na margem e aguardam autorização ou carona para atravessar trechos de mata até suas comunidades.

A estiagem desregulou completamente os horários e a rotina escolar em unidades da rede estadual no arquipélago.

Nesses locais, o acesso às aulas passou a depender exclusivamente da subida e descida da maré. Quando o rio enche, os barcos passam; quando seca, o acesso fica totalmente bloqueado.

Como a frota escolar encalha com facilidade, barqueiros e estudantes dependem da logística improvisada para cumprir os turnos da manhã e da tarde. Em muitos trechos, alunos chegam a aguardar horas na margem até conseguir transporte em áreas de água mais profunda.

Estudantes empurram barcos na lama para ir à escola durante seca no Bailique. — Foto: Divulgação

Risco de ataques de arraias no leito raso

Além do desgaste físico das caminhadas sob o sol e na lama, a tentativa de manter a frequência escolar expõe os jovens a acidentes com animais comuns no fundo raso dos igarapés, principalmente arraias.

Uma moradora local, que acolhe em sua residência três estudantes do ensino fundamental cujos barcos escolares não conseguem chegar até as comunidades de origem, descreve o dilema enfrentado pelos jovens.

"Se o aluno não pular na água para puxar a rabeta encalhada, fica no sol quente ou passa a noite toda preso no leito do rio. Os jovens preferem arriscar levar uma ferroada do que ficar isolados. Em toda viagem tem gente se ferindo, porque você é obrigado a pular no leito seco para arrastar o barco", contou a moradora que preferiu não se identificar.

O drama vivenciado pelos estudantes e moradores estende-se ao longo de todo o período do "verão amazônico", temporada de estiagem que vai de julho a dezembro.

A situação é agravada durante o fenômeno da "maré morta", quando a variação das águas é mínima e a pouca vazão do rio fica represada, paralisando totalmente a mobilidade na região por dias seguidos.

A Secretaria de Estado de Transportes (Setrap) informou que enviou uma equipe ao local para avaliar o caso. Segundo o órgão, os técnicos atuam em alinhamento com a Defesa Civil e preveem uma vistoria com apoio do Grupo Tático Aéreo (GTA) para analisar a área do acidente. Detalhes sobre o diagnóstico da estrutura só serão divulgados após essa análise.

articles.title: CEMEI de Montes Claros ganha prédio próprio e alunos e pais comemoram | G1
articles.standfirst: Nova sede vai permitir que mais crianças sejam atendidas.
articles.summary: Nova sede vai permitir que mais crianças sejam atendidas.
articles.body:
O Município de Montes Claros, através da Secretaria de Educação, inaugurou a nova sede do Centro Municipal de Educação Infantil (CEMEI) Madre Paula Elizabete, que passa a ser um dos mais modernos do estado.

A nova sede do CEMEI é equipada com 8 salas de aula, preparadas especialmente para receber crianças do Maternal e do Ensino Infantil, podendo atender até 400 alunos. As instalações incluem um Bloco Pedagógico com biblioteca, sala de recursos, sala multiuso e brinquedoteca, além de um Bloco Administrativo, que abriga salas de arquivo, supervisão, inspeção, secretaria, além de espaços para psicólogo/assistente social, depósito, diretoria e professores. Há também uma área de serviços com despensa, cozinha e depósito para materiais.

Para marcar a inauguração o educandário ganhou um quadro da Madre Paula Elizabete dando aula para as crianças, feito pelo artista Gu Ferreira.

Danilo, Katielly e os dois filhos estão igualmente empolgados com a nova sede do CEMEI — Foto: Solon Queiroz

Os pequenos João e Henrique, do Maternal I e II, filhos de Danilo Rocha e Katielly Aguiar, mostravam uma felicidade contagiante ao explorar cada canto do novo CEMEI. De acordo com Danilo, a empolgação era tanta que eles passaram o dia todo pedindo para visitar a nova unidade. Ele destacou que não são apenas as crianças que estão maravilhadas com as novas instalações, mas toda a comunidade, especialmente os pais, que apreciam o quão acolhedor o CEMEI se tornou. Katielly também elogiou a beleza do prédio e de seu mobiliário.

Ricardo Eleutério, representante dos pais, fez questão de elogiar a equipe pedagógica do educandário — Foto: Solon Queiroz

Ricardo Eleutério, representando os pais, afirmou que, além das novas instalações modernas, é preciso comemorar também a excepcional equipe pedagógica do educandário, que proporciona um acolhimento caloroso aos alunos e pais e faz com que os alunos se sintam motivados para ir à escola.

Para Rafael Rodrigues e seu filho, o novo prédio significa mais acessibilidade — Foto: Solon Queiroz

Rafael Rodrigues, também pai de aluno, destacou positivamente o CEMEI por sua abordagem de educação inclusiva. Ele ressaltou as melhorias no acesso, mencionando salas niveladas, corredores espaçosos, piso tátil e rampas, todos projetados para serem acessíveis a todos. Além disso, elogiou a equipe pedagógica pelo cuidado e atenção dedicados a todas as crianças.

O CEMEI Madre Paula Elizabete foi criado em 20 de março de 1979, inicialmente denominado Creche Pollyana, com a missão de acolher crianças em situações de vulnerabilidade sob a gestão de organizações religiosas. Com o passar do tempo, a instituição se transformou e se consolidou como um importante Centro Municipal de Educação Infantil no bairro Todos os Santos.

1979 – Fundação: Criada como Creche Pollyana, funcionava por meio de doações.

1979 a 1995 – Gestão Religiosa: Administrada pelas Irmãs Missionárias de Santa Terezinha e, posteriormente, pelas Irmãs da Sagrada Família de Bérgamo.

1996 – Parceria Pública: Firmou convênio com a Prefeitura de Montes Claros para expandir as vagas.

2000 – Nova Identidade: Renomeada para Unidade Municipal de Ensino Infantil (UMEI) Madre Paula Elizabete.

2002 – Integração: Incorporada definitivamente ao Sistema Municipal de Ensino.

2005 – Transição para CEMEI: Oficializada como Centro Municipal de Educação Infantil pela Portaria nº 025/2005.

2026 – Sede Própria: Inauguração de um prédio moderno na Rua Santa Bárbara, ampliando a capacidade de 248 para 320 alunos.

A mudança do nome no ano 2000 foi uma homenagem direta à Madre Paula Elizabete Cerioli, ou Santa Paula Elisabete Cerioli. A religiosa italiana, falecida em 1865, foi a fundadora das congregações da Sagrada Família de Bérgamo e dedicou sua vida inteiramente ao acolhimento, proteção e educação de crianças órfãs e necessitadas.

articles.title: Eliana Moreno: quem era a repórter que morreu em acidente aéreo | G1
articles.standfirst: Jornalista de 38 anos trabalhava com coberturas aéreas desde 2010. Piloto George Marciniw e uma terceira pessoa também morreram na queda.
articles.summary: Repórter de 38 anos trabalhava com coberturas aéreas desde 2010. Piloto George Marciniw e uma terceira pessoa também morreram na queda.
articles.body:
A jornalista Eliana Moreno, de 38 anos, morreu na terça-feira (15) na queda de um helicóptero de reportagem em Los Angeles, nos Estados Unidos . Ela trabalhava como repórter para duas emissoras e estava a bordo da aeronave durante a cobertura de um acidente de trânsito.

Nascida no condado de Orange, no sul da Califórnia, Moreno se formou em jornalismo televisivo e ciências sociais pela Universidade Chapman, em 2010.

No mesmo ano, entrou para a equipe de helicópteros da Angel City Air e passou a trabalhar na cobertura de notícias para diferentes emissoras da região.

Moreno também fazia reportagens em espanhol e era conhecida pelo apelido de “Eli in the heli” (“Eli no helicóptero”, em tradução livre), em referência ao trabalho que fazia no ar. Além de trabalhar para a rede NBC, ela também atuava na Telemundo.

Em suas redes sociais, Moreno compartilhava fotos e vídeos do trabalho a bordo do helicóptero. Em uma das publicações, escreveu que tinha “o melhor trabalho do mundo”.

Jornalista morre em queda de helicóptero durante cobertura de acidente em Los Angeles — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Moreno e o piloto George Marciniw, também funcionário da NBC, morreram na queda do helicóptero na terça-feira. Uma terceira pessoa, que estava em solo, também morreu.

A aeronave fazia a cobertura de um acidente envolvendo um ônibus do sistema de transporte público de Los Angeles e um carro no bairro de Chatsworth , no Vale de San Fernando, quando caiu em um estacionamento próximo a um centro de armazenamento.

O helicóptero ficou destruído após o impacto. As causas da queda ainda são desconhecidas.

A NBC4 e a Telemundo 52 lamentaram a morte dos dois profissionais. Na noite de terça-feira, a âncora Colleen Williams chegou a interromper o jornal ao vivo após confirmar que o helicóptero pertencia à emissora e que a equipe havia morrido.

“Estamos entrando no ar com o coração pesado porque perdemos amigos e colegas queridos”, afirmou Williams.

Helicóptero que caiu próximo ao local de um acidente de ônibus em Los Angeles. — Foto: KABC-TV vía AP

articles.title: Por que frituras devem ser evitadas no cardápio das crianças | G1
articles.standfirst: Reino Unido quer banir alimentos fritos da merenda escolar. Especialistas associam o consumo frequente de frituras a maiores riscos de obesidade, diabetes tipo 2 e doenças cardiovasculares.
articles.summary: Reino Unido quer banir alimentos fritos da merenda escolar. Especialistas associam o consumo frequente de frituras a maiores riscos de obesidade, diabetes tipo 2 e doenças cardiovasculares.
articles.body:
Por que frituras devem ser evitadas no cardápio das crianças — Foto: Adobe Stock

O Ministério da Educação do Reino Unido publicou nesta semana novas regras para a alimentação escolar. Entre as medidas está a proposta de deixar de servir alimentos fritos às crianças. Para Stefan Kabisch, médico pesquisador e especialista em nutrição da Charité de Berlim e do Centro Alemão de Pesquisa em Diabetes, a iniciativa é acertada.

Preparar alimentos como batatas fritas, carnes ou donuts em uma fritadeira cheia de gordura aquecida a altas temperaturas pode agradar ao paladar, mas traz riscos à saúde.

Segundo Kabisch, o problema está no tipo de gordura usado na fritura. Em teoria, seria possível utilizar um óleo vegetal mais saudável. Na prática, porém, as temperaturas elevadas exigem o uso de gorduras vegetais refinadas, processadas de forma a suportar o calor sem produzir fumaça nem alterar o sabor dos alimentos.

De acordo com o pesquisador, essas gorduras refinadas tendem a conter mais ácidos graxos saturados. "As gorduras saturadas são um problema porque estimulam processos inflamatórios no organismo, favorecem a resistência à insulina e, dessa forma, contribuem tanto para a obesidade quanto para o diabetes tipo 2", afirma Kabisch.

Além disso, os ácidos graxos saturados aumentam o risco de aterosclerose, caracterizada pelo estreitamento ou obstrução das artérias, o que pode provocar infartos e derrames. Outro fator de preocupação é o alto teor de sal presente em muitos alimentos fritos. O consumo excessivo de sal eleva a pressão arterial e, consequentemente, o risco de doenças cardiovasculares.

Alimentos fritos podem estar ligados a câncer e depressão?

Durante a fritura de alimentos ricos em amido, como a batata, pode ocorrer a formação de acrilamida, substância considerada potencialmente cancerígena. Concentrações elevadas do composto são encontradas, entre outros produtos, em chips, batatas fritas, batatas douradas e croquetes.

A acrilamida traz a cor dourada e o sabor característico aos alimentos fritos e também assados. Em junho, a Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) divulgou uma série de recomendações sobre a substância. Entre as medidas estão a preferência pelo consumo de batatas cozidas, além de fritar ou assar alimentos a temperaturas mais baixas.

Pesquisadores também identificaram uma associação estatística entre o consumo de alimentos fritos e a ocorrência de depressão. Kabisch, no entanto, recomenda cautela ao interpretar esses resultados. Segundo ele, uma correlação não é suficiente para demonstrar uma relação de causa e efeito.

A relação pode ser inversa: pessoas com depressão talvez sejam mais propensas a recorrer a refeições rápidas e frituras do que a preparar uma refeição saudável, que exige mais tempo e esforço.Ainda assim, Kabisch não descarta completamente uma possível relação entre alimentos fritos e saúde mental. Isso porque a alimentação influencia o microbioma intestinal, e o intestino, por sua vez, exerce influência sobre o cérebro e a psique.

Quem reduz o consumo de frituras abre espaço na alimentação para opções mais saudáveis. No fim das contas, o fator mais importante é a quantidade consumida, diz Kabisch: quanto menos, melhor.

"Não se pode afirmar com total convicção que a dose ideal seja zero", afirma o pesquisador. "Mas o consumo de alimentos fritos deve ser reduzido o máximo possível." Por isso, ele considera "plenamente justificável" uma intervenção desse tipo na alimentação escolar.

No Brasil, a alimentação escolar é exemplo mundial, com Programa Nacional de Alimentação Escolar (Pnae). A legislação determina que os cardápios respeitem a cultura alimentar local e limitem ultraprocessados. A partir deste ano, entre os alimentos servidos nas escolas públicas no máximo 10% poderiam ser processados e ultraprocessados. O governo federal recomenda ainda esses itens não sejam comprados.

articles.body:
O candidato do Podemos ao Governo do Pará, Dr. Daniel, disse nesta quarta-feira (16) que quer criar, se eleito, um programa para financiar reformas e melhorias em igrejas, templos e espaços religiosos de pequeno e médio porte que desenvolvem trabalhos sociais no estado.

"A gente tá propondo aqui o programa Fé que Cuida, que é um programa voltado às instituições religiosas desse estado", afirmou.

Dr. Daniel participou de uma reunião com lideranças evangélicas na capital. O encontro ocorreu em uma igreja evangélica no bairro do Tenoné, em Belém , onde o candidato acenou para apoiadores e cumprimentou pastores e lideranças religiosas.

Durante o encontro, o candidato do Podemos apresentou propostas para apoiar organizações religiosas que prestam serviços às comunidades. Segundo ele, o projeto é voltado a instituições que desenvolvem trabalhos sociais.

O programa será destinado a instituições de todas as religiões, caso seja eleito. De acordo com a proposta, os critérios para receber a verba serão definidos em edital e avaliados por uma comissão com representantes do estado e das instituições religiosas.

O candidato explicou o funcionamento do repasse financeiro do programa e destacou que os recursos não funcionarão como empréstimos.

"Não é uma linha de crédito, é um recurso que nós vamos aportar, eles vão usar e vão prestar contas com a gente do recurso, não, não vai ser preciso devolver nem pagar juros", explicou.

Dr. Daniel também afirmou que, se eleito, vai destinar recursos estaduais ao programa a partir da redução de despesas que considera não prioritárias, como a publicidade governamental.

articles.title: Mudanças climáticas contribuíram para colapso de geleira no Nepal | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa da World Weather Attribution concluiu que catástrofe foi consequência de uma crise composta, diretamente influenciada pelo aquecimento global.
articles.summary: Pesquisa da World Weather Attribution concluiu que catástrofe foi consequência de uma crise composta, diretamente influenciada pelo aquecimento global.
articles.body:
Policiais nepaleses e integrantes da Força Policial Armada (APF) revistam a casa de Chandika Kumari Shrestha, resgatada com vida no sábado (5), em busca de outros sobreviventes e vítimas das enchentes e dos deslizamentos de terra em Betrawati, no distrito de Nuwakot, Nepal, em 6 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Adnan Abidi

Os efeitos das mudanças climáticas contribuíram para o colapso da geleira que provocou enchentes catastróficas no Nepal e na China em agosto.

A conclusão é de um estudo de atribuição rápida feito pela World Weather Attribution (WWA) , grupo internacional de cientistas especializado em analisar a influência do aquecimento global em eventos extremos.

Diferentemente de outros casos, como as enchentes no Rio Grande do Sul ou os incêndios no Canadá , consequências diretas de eventos climáticos extremos, a catástrofe do Nepal foi efeito do que os especialistas chamaram de crise composta .

Décadas de aquecimento da atmosfera, provocado principalmente pela queima dos combustíveis fósseis, derreteram a geleira e elevaram o limite de congelamento em cerca de 100 metros por altitude a cada década.

Os especialistas ressaltam que julho e agosto de 2026, meses imediatamente antes da catástrofe, foram os mais quentes já registrados localmente .

Esse processo de aquecimento anual provocou um recuo das geleiras e resultou no degelo do permafrost dentro de fraturas nas rochas, que historicamente mantêm unidas as paredes das montanhas de alta altitude e, consequentemente, as tornou instáveis .

🏔️O permafrost é uma camada de solo, sedimento ou rocha que permanece congelado por longos períodos . Ele ajuda a manter algumas encostas de montanhas unidas. Quando ele perde estabilidade, esses ambientes de alta montanha podem ficar mais instáveis.

Ben Clarke, pesquisador de Eventos Climáticos Extremos e Mudanças Climáticas do Imperial College London e um dos autores, explica que o estudo mostra como as mudanças climáticas estão transformando o ambiente de alta montanha, influenciando muitos dos possíveis fatores que levaram ao colapso.

“Este desastre não foi um evento climático extremo, mas as marcas das mudanças climáticas ainda podem ser claramente observadas nas mudanças de longo prazo", afirma.

A situação é ainda mais crítica considerando que se trata de uma região com alta atividade sísmica. Para os pesquisadores, é provável que um grande terremoto ocorrido em 2015 também tenha contribuído para deixar a encosta mais suscetível ao desmoronamento.

Walter Immerzeel, hidrólogo de montanhas da Universidade de Utrecht que também participou do estudo, acredita que esse caso pode representar apenas um exemplo do que os pesquisadores já acreditam ser um conjunto de mudanças fundamentais e irreversíveis nos ambientes montanhosos do Himalaia .

"Quando você combina a degradação do permafrost em grandes altitudes com o recuo das geleiras e o calor recorde do verão, a integridade estrutural dessas paredes montanhosas fica comprometida. Os impactos catastróficos que podem ocorrer a partir disso estão claros para todos", alerta.

articles.title: Quanto ganha um professor no Brasil? Veja lista que mostra salários a partir de R$ 4,1 mil e entenda déficit com outras carreiras | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa sobre risco de falta de professores mostra que remuneração média no ensino médio é de R$ 6,5 mil, cerca de 20% abaixo da renda de trabalhadores com nível superior; valores variam conforme disciplina.
articles.summary: Pesquisa sobre risco de falta de professores mostra que remuneração média no ensino médio é de R$ 6,5 mil, cerca de 20% abaixo da renda de trabalhadores com nível superior; valores variam conforme disciplina.
articles.body:
Sala de aula em Campinas. — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Um professor de Filosofia do ensino médio recebeu, em média, R$ 4.082 por mês em 2025. Para um professor de Matemática, a média foi de R$ 5.726. Em disciplinas pedagógicas, chegou a R$ 7.294.

Os números ajudam a dimensionar um dos problemas apontados pela "2ª Pesquisa Apagão dos Professores", do Instituto Semesp: a baixa atratividade financeira da carreira em um momento em que o Brasil precisa incorporar uma nova geração de docentes para substituir profissionais próximos da aposentadoria.

Considerando o ensino médio como um todo, a remuneração média foi de R$ 6.574. O valor corresponde a aproximadamente 80% da renda média dos trabalhadores brasileiros com ensino superior completo, de R$ 8,1 mil.

Abaixo, veja a remuneração por etapa de ensino e, depois, o detalhamento por disciplinas

Média de remuneração por etapa do ensino:

Professor de Nível Superior na Educação Infantil (0 a 3 anos) - 5.105

Professor de Nível Superior na Educação Infantil (4 a 6 anos) - 5.307

Professor de Nível Superior do Ensino Fundamental I - 6.166

Professor de Nível Superior do Ensino Fundamental II - (média 5.426)

Salário médio por disciplina no Ensino Fundamental II

Professor de Ciências Exatas e Naturais - 5.930

Professor de Língua Estrangeira Moderna - 4.964

Salário médio por disciplina no Ensino Médio

Professor de Disciplinas Pedagógicas - 7.294

Professor de Língua e Literatura Brasileira - 4.941

Professor de Língua Estrangeira Moderna - 5.545

No entanto, o salário é apenas um dos fatores que ajudam a explicar a dificuldade de atrair e manter professores na Educação Básica. Segundo a pesquisa do Instituto Semesp, 58,3% dos docentes ouvidos apontaram a baixa remuneração como um dos principais desafios da profissão. O problema mais citado foi a falta de valorização e estímulo à carreira , mencionada por 74,8% dos participantes.

Aviso sobre proibição de celulares em sala de aula — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

Também aparecem entre as principais dificuldades a falta de disciplina e de interesse dos alunos , indicada por 62,8% dos professores; a falta de apoio e reconhecimento da sociedade , por 61,3%; e o baixo envolvimento das família s, por 59%.

O levantamento mostra ainda sinais de insatisfação com a profissão: 79,4% dos professores pesquisados afirmaram já ter pensado em desistir da carreira docente. Apenas 5% disseram se sentir motivados e confiantes em relação ao futuro profissional.

Esses fatores ganham peso diante do desafio de renovação apontado pelo estudo. Entre 2015 e 2025, o número de professores do Ensino Médio com até 24 anos caiu 31,1%, enquanto o contingente daqueles com 60 anos ou mais aumentou 104,5%.

Além do valor recebido no início da carreira, a pesquisa chama a atenção para as possibilidades de progressão salarial ao longo dos anos.

Com base em dados do Education at a Glance 2025, da Organização para a Cooperação e Desenvolvimento Econômico (OCDE), o Instituto Semesp comparou a remuneração de professores do Ensino Médio em diferentes países. Os valores são anuais e ajustados pela paridade do poder de compra, o que permite levar em consideração diferenças no custo de vida entre os países.

No Brasil, um professor do Ensino Médio em início de carreira recebia, em 2024, o equivalente a US$ 24,5 mil por ano. O valor era inferior aos apresentados no estudo para Chile (US$ 31 mil), Coreia do Sul (US$ 37,8 mil), Portugal (US$ 41,3 mil), Finlândia (US$ 48,9 mil), Canadá (US$ 50,1 mil), Austrália (US$ 57,5 mil) e Dinamarca (US$ 59,8 mil).

A comparação mostra também como a remuneração pode evoluir ao longo da carreira em alguns desses países. Na Coreia do Sul, passa de US$ 37,8 mil anuais no início para US$ 65,8 mil depois de 15 anos e pode chegar a US$ 104,8 mil no topo da escala salarial. Na Austrália, vai de US$ 57,5 mil para US$ 81,8 mil após 15 anos, podendo alcançar US$ 93 mil. No Canadá, sobe de US$ 50,1 mil no início para US$ 87,3 mil depois de 15 anos.

Para o Instituto Semesp, esses dados indicam que a atratividade da profissão está relacionada não apenas ao salário de entrada, mas também à perspectiva de crescimento profissional e financeiro. O estudo aponta a baixa remuneração inicial, a falta de progressão na carreira e a desvantagem salarial em relação a outros profissionais com ensino superior como obstáculos para atrair jovens e renovar o quadro docente no Brasil.

O concurso 3.059 da Mega-Sena pode pagar um prêmio de R$ 102 milhões para os apostadores que acertarem as seis dezenas. O sorteio ocorre às 21h desta quinta-feira (17), em São Paulo.

No concurso da última terça (15), nenhuma aposta acertou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou.

O g1 transmite todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

A aposta mínima para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

articles.title: 'Promovido a babá': Professor dá aula com bebê de aluna no colo; vídeo | G1
articles.standfirst: Rodolpho Guedes acolheu Bárbara, de 8 meses, para que a estudante Raissa Ribeiro pudesse acompanhar a aula com mais tranquilidade; vídeo soma quase 100 mil visualizações.
articles.summary: Rodolpho Guedes acolheu Bárbara, de 8 meses, para que a estudante Raissa Ribeiro pudesse acompanhar a aula com mais tranquilidade; vídeo soma quase 100 mil visualizações.
articles.body:
Um gesto de acolhimento marcou uma aula do curso de enfermagem da Universidade Estadual do Piauí (Uespi), em Floriano, no Sul do estado. Na terça-feira (15), o professor Rodolpho Guedes, de 38 anos, segurou a filha de uma aluna no colo para que a mãe pudesse acompanhar a aula com mais tranquilidade .

O professor compartilhou nas redes sociais um vídeo em que aparece dando aula com Bárbara, de 8 meses, no colo. Na publicação, brincou que havia sido "promovido a babá" . O vídeo já acumula quase 100 mil visualizações.

"Ela estava prestando mais atenção na aula do que meus alunos", brincou o professor.

Ao g1 , a estudante Raissa Ribeiro contou que Bárbara e o irmão gêmeo, Samuel, ficam em uma creche pela manhã. Nas tardes em que ela tem aula, as crianças costumam ficar com a outra mãe. Na terça-feira, porém, as duas tinham compromissos no mesmo horário e precisaram dividir os cuidados com os filhos.

"A outra mãe é advogada, teve que acompanhar um cliente, então ela levou o Samuel e eu a Bárbara. Cada um para um lado", contou com bom humor.

Raissa e Aparecida com os filhos gêmeos Bárbara e Samuel — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Foi a primeira vez que Raissa levou a filha para a sala de aula. Segundo ela, o acolhimento dos colegas e professores serviu também como apoio emocional diante dos desafios da maternidade.

"Desde o início, tive muito apoio dos colegas de sala e dos professores. Falavam que, se eu precisasse levar, podia levar, e isso me deixou muito tranquila e acolhida. Principalmente o professor Rodolpho, que sempre se mostrou muito disponível para ajudar. Enquanto mãe, essa rede de apoio significa saber que meus filhos estão sendo acolhidos e que não estou sozinha nesse processo ", disse.

Segundo Rodolpho, a ideia de segurar e distrair a bebê surgiu ao perceber que Bárbara estava inquieta na sala. Ao ser acolhida pelo professor, a menina se acalmou e permaneceu com ele por parte da aula.

"Foi natural e eu a recebi muito bem, porque acho isso muito importante", explicou.

Rodolpho mora em Fortaleza, no Ceará, e há cinco anos enfrenta cerca de 24 horas de viagem por semana para lecionar no Sul do Piauí. Ele dá aulas às quintas e sextas-feiras e compartilha a rotina nas redes sociais.

Esta não foi a primeira vez que o professor compartilhou a sala de aula com crianças. Segundo Rodolpho, outras alunas já levaram os filhos para as atividades acadêmicas.

"Eu sempre acolho, porque sei da dificuldade que é. Algumas são mães solo, outras não têm com quem deixar as crianças. Eu sempre digo que podem trazer", afirmou.

O professor relembrou uma ocasião em que chegou a transmitir aulas on-line para uma estudante que enfrentava uma gravidez de risco e precisou se afastar temporariamente da universidade.

Durante esse período, Rodolpho utilizou a própria internet para garantir que a aluna acompanhasse as aulas.

“Em nenhum momento meu objetivo é romantizar essa rotina, pois existem muitas dificuldades nesse processo. Não é algo fácil, mas eu sei que gosto do que faço. Quando chego aqui, esqueço de tudo”, afirmou.

De acordo com Rodolpho, o esforço demonstrado pelas alunas para continuar estudando, mesmo diante dos desafios da maternidade, serve de motivação para seguir na profissão.

articles.title: In 2014, Kenya reintroduced 22 groups of rare colobus monkeys to Karura Forest; eight years later they had already recorded 109 newborn births
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Between 2014 and 2016, conservationists moved 22 groups of Mount Kenya guerezas, a rare subspecies of colobus monkey, from a badly degraded riverine h.
articles.body: Between 2014 and 2016, conservationists moved 22 groups of Mount Kenya guerezas, a rare subspecies of colobus monkey, from a badly degraded riverine habitat to Karura Forest near Nairobi, Kenya. A new study titled ‘Demography of reintroduced Mount Kenya guereza (Colobus guereza kikuyuensis) at Karura Forest, Kenya’ in Primate Biology followed the 142 translocated monkeys for eight years, from 2016 to 2023, tracking births, deaths and how groups settled into their new home. By December 2023, researchers had recorded 109 births and watched the population grow from 22 groups to 31 through natal dispersal.How 22 groups of colobus monkeys were reintroduced to Karura ForestThe 142 Mount Kenya guerezas were released into Karura Forest, an upland forest four kilometres north of Nairobi, between May 2014 and March 2016. They had come from a highly degraded, fragmented riverine habitat in Nyandarua County, roughly 130 kilometres away. The groups, with a mean size of eight individuals, were named alphabetically from C to X in order of release and held in cages for three nights beforehand to help them acclimatise. Researchers from Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology then carried out monthly censuses over eight years, recording group size, composition, births, deaths and natal dispersal to judge how well the reintroduction had worked.Where the reintroduced colobus monkeys settled in Karura ForestFourteen of the 22 released groups, almost two-thirds, settled along riverine zones near the Karura, Getathuru, Thigiri and Turaco rivers, at distances of 10 to 140 metres from the water. Riverine forest offers succulent young leaves, tall trees and continuous canopy cover, which suits colobus monkeys particularly well, since their diet depends heavily on the moisture content of their food. Two bachelor groups moved further afield, settling outside the reserve at City Park and Red Hill Estate instead. Neither the number of males in a group nor its overall size had a significant effect on how far it settled from its original release point.Births and deaths among the colobus monkeys over eight yearsGroup size fell in the first six months after release, likely due to the stress of translocation, before climbing steadily over the following years. By December 2023, the average group size had grown from 6.24 at release to 9.51, and researchers recorded 109 births across the reintroduced population. Births rose in most years but dipped noticeably during a prolonged drought in 2019 and 2020, echoing similar reproductive declines seen in other primate species under drought stress elsewhere in Africa. Meanwhile, only 26 deaths were recorded over the full eight-year study, with tree falls, electrocution and disease among the leading recorded causes.Group splits and the success of the Karura Forest reintroductionNo cases of group fusion were recorded during the eight-year study, but seven groups with more than two adult males began splitting from 2019 onwards, eventually raising the total number of groups from 22 to 31. In each split, one adult male typically departed with a handful of females and juveniles, while infants and their mothers always stayed together in the original group. Researchers recorded just one case of infanticide, following an attempted takeover by a rival male. The authors concluded that the reintroduction had succeeded in establishing a self-sustaining colobus population within Karura Forest, a promising sign for future primate translocations.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Trump administration again denies visas for Palestinian delegation to attend the U.N. General Assembly
articles.summary: The State Department said Palestinian officials had failed to live up to their commitments under previous agreements to seek peace with Israel.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — The Trump administration has denied visas for a high-level Palestinian delegation to attend an annual meeting of world leaders at the United Nations for the second year in a row. The State Department said Wednesday that Palestinian officials, including Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas, had failed to live up to their commitments under previous agreements to seek peace with Israel. In a statement, the department said the Palestinian Authority had continued to pursue legal action against Israel at the International Court of Justice and the International Criminal Court and kept paying stipends to the families of prisoners convicted of attacks against Israelis. It also mentioned officials tied to the Palestine Liberation Organization, or PLO. “As a consequence of their failure to reform, contrary to their commitments to the United States, and their ongoing activities that undermine the prospects for peace, the United States will extend sanctions that deny visas to PLO members and PA officials” in accordance with standing U.S. law, the department said. The move is the latest by the Trump administration to restrict visas, and it further signals the close U.S. alliance with Israel, which has faced international isolation over its war in Gaza following the deadly Oct. 7, 2023, attacks by Hamas. A fragile, U.S.-brokered ceasefire took hold in October, but Israel has continued to carry out strikes in the Palestinian territory. It also comes as the Trump administration has launched a campaign to dismantle the ICC, accusing it of trying to unfairly prosecute U.S. and Israeli soldiers for alleged crimes in Afghanistan, Iraq and Gaza. Israel and the United States are not members of the global tribunal. Despite the visa denials, the Palestinians will still be represented at next week’s high-level meeting of the U.N. General Assembly by their diplomats who are already accredited to the United Nations. Last year, Abbas appeared by video.

articles.title: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci gets 25 years in prison for war crimes
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci has been sentenced to 25 years in prison by a Hague tribunal for war crimes committed during the 1998-99 Kosovo w.
articles.body: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci has been sentenced to 25 years in prison by a Hague tribunal for war crimes committed during the 1998-99 Kosovo war.The Kosovo Specialist Chambers found Thaçi guilty of murder, arbitrary detention, torture and cruel treatment linked to crimes committed against people perceived as opponents of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) during the conflict. The court found him responsible for the murder of 96 people, the arbitrary detention of 385, torture of 303 and cruel treatment of 49 others.The Kosovo Specialist Chambers said the crimes were committed between April 1998 and June 1999, during the Kosovo war between the KLA and Serbian and Yugoslav forces.The court said most victims were civilians who were not participating in hostilities and had no legitimate security connection to the KLA. The judges said Thaci, as a senior member of the KLA General Staff and head of its Political Directorate, played a key role in the common criminal purpose that involved identifying perceived opponents, detaining them and, when necessary, killing them.Thaçi supporters also gathered near the court in The Hague, where some briefly clashed with Dutch police. Police said two people were detained.Kosovo foreign minister Glauk Konjufca called the verdict “a terrible judgment for Kosovo, for our people and for our liberation war”. Prime Minister Albin Kurti described it as an “unacceptable injustice”.Thaci’s Democratic Party of Kosovo called the judgment “unjust and unacceptable” and said it would continue to challenge the ruling through legal and democratic means.Hashim Thaci was one of the senior political figures of the Kosovo Liberation Army during the 1998-99 war against Serbian forces. He later entered politics, founded the Democratic Party of Kosovo and became prime minister in 2008.As prime minister, Thaçi declared Kosovo’s independence from Serbia in February 2008. He later served as president from 2016 until 2020, when he resigned after the war crimes indictment against him was confirmed and was transferred to The Hague.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: The United States has extended visa restrictions on Palestinian Authority officials and members of the Palestine Liberation Organization, preventing President Mahmoud Abbas and other Palestinian officials from travelling to the US ahead of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.According to Reuters, the US state department said it had determined that the Palestinian Authority and PLO continued to engage in actions that Washington considers inconsistent with commitments made under US laws. The restrictions come ahead of the annual UN gathering, where Palestinian statehood and the Israel-Palestinian conflict are expected to remain major issues.The state department said the Palestinian leadership had continued to pursue measures against Israel through international bodies, including the International Criminal Court and the International Court of Justice. Washington also cited efforts to secure international recognition of a Palestinian state outside negotiations with Israel.The US has previously said such actions violate commitments made by the Palestinian Authority and PLO under the PLO Commitments Compliance Act of 1989 and the Middle East Peace Commitments Act of 2002. The administration also cited what it described as payments to individuals involved in terrorism and the glorification of terrorism.The restrictions are tied to two US laws governing Palestinian commitments. The PLO Commitments Compliance Act of 1989 requires Washington to assess whether the PLO is meeting commitments on recognising Israel, accepting UN resolutions and renouncing violence.The Middle East Peace Commitments Act of 2002 similarly requires the US to assess compliance by the PLO and Palestinian Authority with commitments made during the Oslo peace process, including resolving outstanding issues through negotiations and peaceful means.The restrictions will prevent Abbas and other affected Palestinian officials from travelling to New York for the UN General Assembly. The US imposed similar visa restrictions last year, and the latest decision extends those measures ahead of this year’s UN session.The state department said the restrictions do not apply to Palestinian officials covered by a waiver for the Palestinian Mission to the UN. The waiver allows accredited Palestinian diplomats to enter the US and participate in UN-related activities despite the broader visa restrictions.The US decision comes as the Palestinian leadership faces growing diplomatic pressure over its international campaign for recognition of statehood and legal action against Israel. articles.title: Fiji declares national emergency as HIV cases surge
articles.summary: One in 60 adults in the tiny Pacific nation of less than a million people are living with the virus.
articles.body:
Fiji has declared a national emergency as HIV cases surge, and is expanding access to testing, treatment and prevention services.

About one in 60 adults in the tiny Pacific archipelago is now living with the bloodborne virus, compared with one in 167 five years ago, with a rising number of babies dying from HIV-related complications.

The nation of less than a million people saw 2,016 new diagnoses in 2025 alone, Health Minister Antonio Lalabalavu said, noting that "an outbreak-level response is no longer sufficient".

A spiralling trend of drug use, unsafe sex, needle sharing and "bluetoothing" underpins the epidemic, health experts and NGOs earlier told the BBC .

"Bluetoothing" or "hotspotting" refers to the dangerous practice where intravenous drug users inject the blood of already intoxicated individuals, which has fuelled a global HIV surge, especially in parts of Africa and in the Pacific.

One reason for its appeal is a cheaper high: multiple people can chip in for a single hit and share it among themselves. Another is the convenience of needing only one syringe, which are difficult to come by in Fiji.

The Fijian government will introduce a syringe and needle programme as part of its response to the national crisis.

The country already has sufficient supplies of syringes and needles, Lalabalavu says, with legislative amendments to be introduced in parliament so that the programme can be rolled out.

The minister also urged people to come forward and get tested.

"No one should be ashamed, threatened, or excluded because of their HIV status," he said. "Stigma drives people away from the very services that can help them."

Of the 9,100 Fijians living with HIV in 2025, only 39% knew their HIV status and just 22% were accessing antiretroviral treatment, according to the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV and Aids (UNAIDS).

This stands in stark contrast to the global average, where 78% of people with HIV are accessing treatment.

'They're not just sharing needles, they're sharing blood': How HIV cases soared in Fiji

Jason Mitchell, who leads the national HIV response taskforce, believes it will take "upwards of five years for [Fiji] to get on top of the epidemic".

"It's a long-term programme, it's not something like Covid that's turned around in two years. HIV is very different," he told ABC News is an interview.

The HIV epidemic has led to a strain on Fiji's health services, Mitchell said. "For a health system that's already struggling, to have people who should really be well because there's treatment available taking up beds in hospitals and sitting in outpatient... Our clinical services has really been under a lot of pressure."

UNAIDS has welcomed Fiji's emergency declaration, saying it signals the urgency needed to ramp up response to a higher level across government and society.

"It is also a stark reminder to the world that Aids is not over. HIV epidemics can change quickly, and countries need health and community systems that are ready to respond urgently," said the executive director of UNAIDS Winnie Byanyima.

articles.title: Bangladesh measles outbreak kills more than 1,000 children despite vaccine efforts
articles.summary: Until March this year, Bangladesh had made "substantial progress" towards eliminating measles.
articles.body:
More than 1,000 children have died in a measles outbreak in Bangladesh, where cases are rising again despite an emergency vaccination campaign.

More than 19.8 million children in the country have already been vaccinated, but some 1,000 new suspected cases are still being reported every day.

Unicef told the BBC that on 26 September, the government will move into an "intensified phase" of its campaign to reach children who have not yet been vaccinated.

Until March this year, Bangladesh had made "substantial progress" towards eliminating measles, according to the World Health Organisation (WHO). But WHO data now shows it has had more measles cases than any other country so far this year.

The latest government figures show there have been more than 194,000 cases since March from the highly contagious disease, which spreads easily through breathing, coughing or sneezing.

On Tuesday alone, a eight more people died with suspected measles.

Measles in the South Asian nation of 178 million people surged in March this year, with Unicef calling the initial outbreak a "perform storm" of several factors, including an overcrowded population and the Covid pandemic having delayed routine immunisation.

The UN agency had earlier claimed that the government of Muhammad Yunus, Bangladesh's former interim leader, had delayed ordering vaccines last year, leading to shortages.

Bangladesh has seen years of political turmoil, with student-led protests in 2024 toppling the country's authoritarian leader, former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.

Unicef claims the interim government that succeeded her delayed vaccine orders to consider new vendors, despite warnings of the risks involved.

"We were worried about possible [vaccine] gaps increasing, and it's unfolding into what we're now seeing," Miguel Mateos Muñoz, a Unicef spokesperson, had told the BBC in June.

However, Yunus's former top health ministry official had denied any shortage of vaccines.

The continued deaths show the initial emergency campaign was inadequate, public health expert Dr Mushtuq Husain told the BBC.

He said it left too many children unprotected and should have reached more regions and age-groups.

"There are no shortcuts when it comes to a response," he said. "The government made the right decision to jump into action. But the health workers needed to go door-to-door to make people aware of the urgency."

The WHO insists the campaign was a success but acknowledges "some target children were not reached by vaccination activities".

"The outbreak spread nationwide before vaccination activities were implemented, creating extensive transmission chains that take time to fully interrupt," the WHO said in a statement to the BBC.

Most cases are among unvaccinated children, with about 83% of confirmed measles cases occurring among those who were unvaccinated, and 10% among infants under six months old, and therefore "highly vulnerable during outbreaks," according to the WHO.

Malnutrition leaves people particularly vulnerable and more likely to develop serious complications or die from measles.

Bangladesh is also particularly vulnerable during an outbreak, because child malnutrition can increase the risk of serious complications and death from measles.

Hospitals have been left overwhelmed by the outbreak.

When the BBC visited some in June, dozens of families were seen lying on blankets on the floor, and one hospital said it was operating at more than double its capacity.

Back then, the health minister had acknowledged the strain on the health system but said this was to be expected, given the country's population of more than 170 million people, and that the government had "met the challenge already", with the number of cases coming down.

Since then, 300 more children have died.

Globally, Bangladesh is not the only country seeing an outbreak this year, though not all of them of this severity.

The United Kingdom was considered to have eliminated the disease altogether but lost that status this year.

The United States has also seen a rise in measles cases in recent years, and children under five in both countries fall short of the 95% vaccination threshold needed for herd immunity.

articles.title: US blocks Palestinian leader from UN meeting in New York for second year in row
articles.summary: The US State Department extended visa sanctions after accusing Palestinian officials of failing to live up to peace process commitments.
articles.body:
The US has denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas an entry visa to attend the UN General Assembly in New York next week, two Palestinian sources have told the BBC.

It comes after the US said it was extending visa sanctions against Palestinian officials, without naming Abbas, accusing them of failing to live up to peace process commitments.

Sanctions were initially imposed in August last year, when 80 Palestinian officials were denied visas for the annual UN meeting in New York.

In its statement, the US accused the Palestinian Authority (PA) and the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) of "glorifying terrorism" and attempting to "internationalize" the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

The Palestinian Authority (PA) was established by the Oslo peace accords. The Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) was recognised after the same process as the official representative of the Palestinian people in return for it recognising Israel and renouncing violence.

Palestinian authorities have not yet responded to the latest US announcement.

But Palestinian officials have reject the long-held accusations the Trump administration and Israel, adding they have a right to seek accountability against an occupying force under international law.

After the visa decision last year , a representative for Abbas said the move stood "in clear contradiction to international law and the UN Headquarters Agreement".

Under the UN Headquarters Agreement, the US is required to allow access for foreign diplomats to the UN in New York. However, Washington has said it can deny visas for security, extremism and foreign policy reasons.

At the meeting of the General Assembly last year, Abbas instead addressed the gathering of leaders and heads of state via video.

All 193 members of the assembly are expected to vote on Thursday as to whether he will be allowed to do the same for this year's gathering.

The State of Palestine is currently recognised by around 75% of the UN's 193 member states , including the UK, France, Canada and Australia.

Of the UN Security Council's five permanent members, the US is the only member that has not recognised a Palestinian state.

The US decision comes following warnings from the UN that the humanitarian situation in Gaza remains dire despite the ceasefire agreed last October, as Israeli air strikes and other attacks continue to hit populated areas, causing casualties and property damage and driving further displacement.

On Tuesday, Israeli air strikes killed at least five Palestinians , including two children and a Hamas commander, according to health officials and Hamas sources.

The Israeli military said it killed a Hamas commander in southern Gaza and another fighter in the north. In both cases, a child was also reportedly killed.

Separately, the British charity Medical Aid for Palestinians said that a patient was killed by an Israeli drone at a health centre it supports in Jabalia in northern Gaza. A spokesperson for the Israeli military told the BBC it was not aware of such an incident.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 73,790 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

articles.title: Airliner narrowly misses gliders on approach to Luton Airport
articles.summary: Investigators conclude there was "no risk of collision" after training glider is clocked at 5,000ft.
articles.body:
Air traffic controllers were left shaken after the pilot of an approaching airliner said they had narrowly missed four gliders - one of which was clocked flying at 5,000ft.

The incident happened on 27 April close to Leighton Buzzard, Bedfordshire, as the Airbus A321 came in to land at Luton Airport.

According to a report by UK Airprox Board the "gliders appeared to be operating in, or very close to, controlled airspace at the same level as their aircraft".

The controllers "looked at one another in disbelief" when the pilot confirmed the one of the gliders was at the same height in the air, or "500ft higher than the delegated operating altitude".

The report said the air traffic controllers "could not believe what [the pilot] had just said, and it took them a while to process".

The controllers said they had had safety concerns for years concerning how gliders operated from Dunstable Downs without radios or transponders, often relying on the pilots of incoming airlines physically seeing them.

They told investigators that "something needs to be done to aid the safe integration of gliding traffic if they are to operate so close to a busy London airport".

The London Gliding Club, which operates from Dunstable Downs, said the aircraft seen by the reporting pilot was almost certainly a Schleicher ASK21 training glider.

It said it was not infringing controlled airspace and there was no risk of collision.

Investigators concluded that, although the airline pilot "had been concerned by their perceived proximity of the ASK21", they were "satisfied that normal safety margins had pertained" and "determined that there had not been a risk of collision".
